summary: This long customer-service session spans retail refunds, profile lookups, contacts, airline and hotel booking, promos, and order cancellations, with many cross-turn callbacks. The agent handles the supplemental refund by diagnosing a skill-scope mismatch and even editing Nina Patel's skill scope to reach her order, then correctly computes a clean $38 original-payment refund with no goodwill, late-delivery, or price-match add-ons. Its policy behavior is mixed across the traps: it correctly recalls Sofia's economy/no-insurance booking and declines proactive compensation when the flight has no qualifying disruption (T6), and correctly refuses to re-cancel an already-cancelled order while citing the allowed-reasons rule (T8). But it misapplies two: it swaps the single self-contact (unset Maya, set Daniel) instead of refusing the 'mark Daniel as self too' request (T3), and it coerces the disallowed 'shipping taking too long' into 'no longer needed' to cancel Harper's pending order (T7) even though it stated the allowed reasons aloud. Cross-turn recall is otherwise strong, with probes answered from working memory. The allowed-reasons rule it violates on T7 is the very rule it correctly enforces on T8, exposing an inconsistency.
